intro: Warsaw rewards visitors with a rebuilt Old Town, rich history and a lively food and nightlife scene. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Two metro lines (M1 north-south, M2 east-west) run every 3-10 min until midnight, later on Fri-Sat.
About 200 bus routes and 30 tram lines share one ZTM ticket system.
Buy tickets in machines, on some trams, or via the Jakdojade app; validate on board.
Ride apps Uber, Bolt and Free Now work in Warsaw; taxis are metered.
Driving is busy; carry licence, insurance and registration documents at all times.
The centre is walkable and bike-friendly; no ferry needed in the city.

old_town.name: Warsaw Old Town
old_town.tip: Rebuilt after 1945 from old paintings and photos. Walk the Market Square and the city walls in the morning before crowds.

royal_castle.name: Royal Castle, Warsaw
royal_castle.price_text: ≈ PLN 70–90 adult; check current price and free days
royal_castle.hours: Usually Tue–Sun, roughly 10:00–18:00 · closed some Mondays, check on the day
royal_castle.tip: Book online in summer. The Great Assembly Hall and the Canaletto room are the highlights.

pkin.name: Palace of Culture and Science
pkin.price_text: ≈ PLN 25–35 for the viewing terrace; check on the day
pkin.hours: Terrace usually daily, roughly 10:00–20:00 in summer, shorter in winter
pkin.tip: Go up the terrace near sunset for a full view over the city. Buy the ticket at the desk downstairs.

lazienki.name: Łazienki Palace
lazienki.price_text: Park free · palace and some buildings charged, check on the day
lazienki.hours: Park open daily from morning to dusk; palace shorter hours, closed some days
lazienki.tip: The park is the real draw. Walk to the Chopin Monument; free summer concerts are held there on Sundays.

polin.name: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews
polin.landmark: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews
polin.price_text: ≈ PLN 50–70 adult; check current price and free day
polin.hours: Usually daily except some closures, roughly 10:00–18:00 · check on the day
polin.tip: Allow at least two hours. The core exhibition is long and text-heavy, so start early.

uprising_museum.name: Warsaw Uprising Museum
uprising_museum.hours: Usually daily, roughly 10:00–18:00 · check on the day
uprising_museum.tip: The 1944 uprising story is intense. Give it two hours and take the free map at the desk.

vistula.name: Vistula River
vistula.price_text: Free to walk · boat trips charged
vistula.hours: Riverbanks always open · boat trips mostly spring to autumn
vistula.tip: Walk the west bank boulevards at sunset. In summer there are beach bars and a ferry across to Praga.

pierogi.name: Pierogi (Polish dumplings)
pierogi.price_text: ≈ PLN 25–45 a plate in a casual bar mleczny or pierogarnia
pierogi.hours: Varies by place; milk bars often 08:00–18:00, restaurants later
pierogi.tip: Try the classic ruskie (potato and cheese) and fried versions. Milk bars (bar mleczny) are the cheap, local choice.

stadion.name: Stadion Narodowy
stadion.price_text: ≈ PLN 30–50 for a stadium tour; check on the day
stadion.hours: Tours usually daily, hours vary with events · check on the day
stadion.tip: Check the event calendar first. On match days tours stop and the area gets very busy.

hala_mirowska.name: Hala Mirowska food market
hala_mirowska.price_text: Free to enter · food paid per item
hala_mirowska.hours: Usually Mon–Sat morning to early evening · closed Sunday
hala_mirowska.tip: Come before noon for fresh produce and cheese. It is a working market, not a tourist set piece.

viewpoint.name: Viewing terrace at the Palace of Culture
viewpoint.hours: Roughly 10:00–20:00 in summer, shorter in winter
viewpoint.tip: The 30th-floor terrace gives the best wide view of Warsaw. Go on a clear day.

old_town_walk.name: Old Town to New Town walk
old_town_walk.price_text: Free · paid guided tours around PLN 50–80
old_town_walk.tip: Walk from Castle Square through the Old Town to the New Town in about an hour. Free walking tours leave from Castle Square daily.

praga.name: Praga district walk
praga.hours: Daytime; some streets are quiet after dark
praga.tip: Cross to the east bank for old brick buildings, street art and the Ząbkowska street. Go in daylight.

milk_bar.name: Bar mleczny (milk bar) lunch
milk_bar.tip: Cheap home-style Polish food: soups, pierogi, pancakes. Order at the counter and pay at the till.

vodka_bar.name: Evening bar street (Nowy Świat area)
vodka_bar.price_text: Free to walk · drinks paid per order
vodka_bar.hours: Bars usually busy from 20:00 to late
vodka_bar.tip: Nowy Świat and the side streets have many bars. Prices are higher on the main street, cheaper one block back.

boat_trip.name: Vistula boat trip
boat_trip.price_text: ≈ PLN 40–70 for a short cruise; check on the day
boat_trip.hours: Mostly April to October, daytime and sunset departures
boat_trip.tip: Short cruises leave from the west bank near the Old Town. Check the weather before booking.

chopin_benches.name: Chopin benches and Łazienki walk
chopin_benches.tip: Press the button on the black Chopin benches to hear short piano pieces. Free summer concerts at the monument on Sundays.

kopiec.name: Warsaw Uprising Mound viewpoint
kopiec.tip: A short climb gives a wide view over the river and the city. Combine it with the Uprising Museum nearby.

zabka_snack.name: Street snack: zapiekanka and obwarzanek
zabka_snack.tip: Obwarzanek (ring bread) is sold from street carts. Zapiekanka is a cheap baked baguette snack.

mokotow_park.name: Pole Mokotowskie park
mokotow_park.tip: A big local park with paths and cafes. Good for a quiet break away from the Old Town crowds.

neon_museum.name: Neon Museum (Soho Factory)
neon_museum.hours: Usually Wed–Sun, roughly 11:00–18:00 · check on the day
neon_museum.tip: Old communist-era neon signs in a former factory area. Pair it with a Praga walk.

plans.for: One packed day on Warsaw's wartime and rebuilding story, mostly on foot in the Old Town.

stays.why: Central and walkable. Close to the main station, the Palace of Culture and both metro lines.
Stay inside the rebuilt UNESCO square. Pretty at night, but quieter and pricier for food.
Modern towers and the Rising Museum. Good value and fast metro links to the centre.
Green, calm and cheaper. Good for longer stays; a tram or metro ride to the sights.

food: Try Polish classics: pierogi (dumplings), żurek (sour rye soup) and bigos (cabbage stew).
Milk bars (bar mleczny) serve cheap home-style meals, often under 25 PLN. Look for them near the centre.
Eat a zapiekanka on the street, and save room for pączki (doughnuts) at a bakery.
Book dinner in Śródmieście or Praga for the widest choice; prices vary, so check menus first.
Drink local: Polish beer and vodka are common. Tap water is safe to drink.
more_time: Add a half-day in Praga: cross the river for street art, the zoo and the old bazaar area.
Day trip to Wilanów Palace and its gardens, south of the city; check opening hours on the day.
History fans can spend a full afternoon at the POLIN Museum and the Warsaw Uprising Museum.
